walkthroughs.body_html:
Legal Moral & Ethical Issues — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Legal Moral & Ethical Issues brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Legal Moral & Ethical Issues.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 primarily regulates:
options: Surveillance and interception of communications by public bodies
The price of broadband contracts
Copyright on musical works
Health and safety in offices

mcqs.q: The Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 protects:
options: Original works, including software, from unauthorised copying
Computers from physical theft
Personal data held by companies
Employees from unfair dismissal

mcqs.q: Creating and distributing malware to impair computers is an offence under:
options: The Data Protection Act 2018
The Computer Misuse Act 1990
The Freedom of Information Act 2000
The Equality Act 2010
The gap between those with effective access to digital technology and skills and those without
The split between analogue and digital broadcasting
Dividing a hard disk into partitions
The difference between binary 0 and 1

mcqs.q: Is illegally copying music an offence under the Computer Misuse Act?
options: Yes - the Computer Misuse Act covers any illegal activity involving a computer.
Yes - the digital divide refers to splitting files between two disks.
Yes - music piracy is covered by the Data Protection Act.
No - unauthorised copying of creative works falls under the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988; the Computer Misuse Act covers unauthorised access and damage to systems.

mcqs.q: Does personal data only mean secret or sensitive information?
options: Yes - data stops being personal once it is posted online.
Yes - music piracy is covered by the Data Protection Act.
No - personal data is any information relating to an identified or identifiable living person, including names, email addresses and online identifiers.
Yes - only secrets like medical records count as personal data.

mcqs.q: Is the digital divide only about who owns devices?
options: No - it also covers differences in connectivity quality, digital skills and confidence, so someone with a device may still be digitally excluded.
Yes - once everyone has a smartphone the divide is closed.
Yes - data stops being personal once it is posted online.
Yes - the digital divide refers to splitting files between two disks.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Data Protection Act 2018”?
options: The gap between people who have effective access to digital technology and skills and those who do not, creating social and economic inequality.
UK law, alongside UK GDPR, governing how organisations process personal data, requiring fairness, accuracy, security and a lawful basis.
UK law regulating the powers of public bodies to carry out surveillance and to intercept electronic communications.
UK law protecting original creative works, including software and music, from being copied or distributed without the rights holder's permission.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Computer Misuse Act 1990”?
options: UK law, alongside UK GDPR, governing how organisations process personal data, requiring fairness, accuracy, security and a lawful basis.
The gap between people who have effective access to digital technology and skills and those who do not, creating social and economic inequality.
The individual's interest in controlling personal information; data gathering, tracking and surveillance technologies raise both legal and moral questions.
UK law criminalising unauthorised access to computer material, access with intent to commit further offences, and impairing computers, including with malware.
